change_interpretations.engineering_summary: The allowed driver torque response time has been reduced from 100 ms to 80 ms, tightening the performance objective; verification must demonstrate torque command within 80 ms for pedal demands >70 %.

assessments.reason: The test measures driver torque response time; procedure expects ≤100 ms and recorded 94 ms, which passes the old limit but exceeds the new 80 ms limit.
assessments.recommended_action: Update the procedure to use an 80 ms threshold and rerun the test to obtain a measurement that meets the tightened limit.

assessments.reason: The test references VCU-DR-01 but only checks priority arbitration and does not record response time; the tighter 80 ms limit may require adding a timing check.
evidence: Comment: Timing not reported in old evidence
assessments.recommended_action: Have the test owner decide whether to extend the test to capture torque response time and update the procedure accordingly.

assessments.reason: The test records a maximum response of 92 ms, which passes the old 100 ms limit but violates the new 80 ms limit.
assessments.recommended_action: Revise the acceptance threshold to 80 ms and rerun the high‑load transient test.

assessments.reason: The test validates brake actuator latency (VCU-BRK-03) and does not involve driver torque response timing.
evidence: Procedure target 100 ms for brake command
assessments.recommended_action: No action required for this change.

assessments.reason: The test checks wheel‑speed sensor failure handling (VCU-DGN-04), unrelated to torque response time.
The test audits mode change logging (VCU-LOG-05) and does not address driver torque response.
The test has no linked requirement and does not explicitly measure torque response time; its relevance to the tightened limit cannot be established.
assessments.recommended_action: No immediate action; keep under review if future linkage is added.

assessments.reason: The test references an unknown legacy requirement and validates diagnostic replay, not driver torque response.
The test compares torque ramps between modes (VCU-MOD-06) and contains no quantitative response‑time assertion.
The test validates pedal‑signal spike filtering (VCU-DR-02) and does not involve response‑time measurement.
The test checks brake priority over torque (VCU-BRK-03) and does not measure torque response latency.
The test verifies ECU wake‑up timing, unrelated to driver torque response.
The test measures response at 60 % demand, recorded 86 ms; exceeds the new 80 ms limit.
assessments.recommended_action: Adjust the acceptance criterion to 80 ms and rerun the low‑demand step response test.
